It began on 11 March and ended on 18 November.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesk/kenya2017.html Kenya 2017], RSSSF.com [[Tusker F.C.|Tusker]] was the defending champions, going into the season on the back of their 11th league title.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}} The Kenyan Premier League was expanded to 18 teams, of which 14 returned from the [[2016 Kenyan Premier League|2016 season]]. [[F.C. Kariobangi Sharks|Kariobangi Sharks]], [[Nakumatt F.C.|Nakumatt]], [[Nzoia Sugar F.C.|Nzoia Sugar]] (formerly Nzoia United) and [[Zoo Kericho F.C.|Zoo Kericho]] were promoted from the second-tier [[2016 in Kenyan football#National Super League|National Super League]]. On 21 October 2017, [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] secured their record 16th league title with four games to spare after beating [[Ulinzi Stars F.C.|Ulinzi Stars]] 3–1 at the Kericho Green Stadium.{{cite web|url=http://www.nation.co.ke/sports/football/Gor-Mahia-gun-down-Ulinzi-to-clinch-KPL-title/1102-4149802-1vrop3/index.html |title=Ulinzi Stars 0-1 Gor Mahia: Kagere strikes to hand K'Ogalo 16th title |date=21 October 2017 |author=Vincent Opiyo |work=[[Daily Nation]] |access-date=22 October 2017}} ==Changes from last season== {{location map+ |Kenya |float=right |width=380 |caption=Locations of the 2017 Kenyan Premier League teams.|places= {{location map~ |Kenya |lat=-4.045006 |long=39.666154 |label=
